In this insightful episode of the Charles Mizrahi Show, we welcome back Mark Mills, a renowned energy expert and senior fellow at the Manhattan Institute. Join us as we explore the intricate relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) and energy consumption, and the significant impact this has on our future. Mark is also the author of The Cloud Revolution: How the Convergence of New Technologies Will Unleash the Next Economic Boom and A Roaring 2020s
Mark shares his recent testimony before the U.S. Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources, providing a firsthand account of the challenges and opportunities at the intersection of AI and energy. We delve into the practical realities of electric vehicles (EVs) and renewable energy sources, discussing the hurdles that need to be overcome for a successful transition.
The conversation also covers the massive energy demands of data centers, which are poised to grow even further with the advancement of AI technologies.

AI has many amygdalae flooding nervous systems with warnings; a rising share of Americans look toward digital technology with deep suspicion; and a data center revolt is underway. The worries are increasingly apocalyptic. But it's not that America has never experienced a transformation of comparable scale, only that no living American is old enough to remember it—or so argues today's guest: Mark Mills, author of The Cloud Revolution: How the Convergence of New Technologies Will Unleash the Next Economic Boom and A Roaring 2020s . Mark, the erudite optimist, addresses everything from the cold realities behind development, construction, and energy considerations to productivity gains, labor participation, sociocultural cohesion, and cybersecurity risks.
Plus, while on the subject of the tumultuous present, James, Steve and Charles reflect on Ryan Reynolds' thoughts on the traumatic 1980s; Steve thinks through a proposal to curb bad actors in the "non-profit sector"; and while they look forward to cutting the rug at the White House's new ballroom, the trio find themselves baffled by Chief Justice Robert's sudden fretting over standing.

About the author

Mark Mills graduated from Cambridge University in 1986. He has lived in both Italy and France, and has written for the screen. His first novel, 'The Whaleboat House', won the 2004 Crime Writer's Association for Best Novel by a debut author. His second, 'The Savage Garden', was a Richard and Judy Summer Read and No 1 bestseller. He lives in Oxford with his wife and two children.

Making Your Mark with Mark Mills

The Exceptional Sales Leader Podcast
06-10-2026 • 1 hora
In this episode of the Exceptional Sales Leader Podcast, I am joined by Mark Mills OBE, a distinguished entrepreneur from the UK, who has founded and sold five successful businesses. Mark shares his path from a young entrepreneur selling broken biscuits to a business mogul owning Cardpoint, a prominent independent cash machine company. Both lighthearted and informative, the episode dives into the challenges and triumphs Mark faced, offering an abundance of wisdom for aspiring entrepreneurs. He provides an enriching perspective on the importance of perseverance and refining business models, emphasising, “Failure cannot live with persistence.” He discusses various business ventures, including how an ordinary petrol stop and a US trip led to groundbreaking ideas. For Mark, entrepreneurship isn’t just about profit but adaptability and integrity. His insights offer a blueprint for identifying not only profitable ventures but also a deep sense of purpose beyond just financial success.
